html:
The Sanapaná are an Indigenous people of the Gran Chaco in western Paraguay. They lived as mobile hunters, gatherers and small farmers on the dry plains and palm savannas west of the Paraguay River.

Their language belongs to the Enlhet-Enenlhet (Mascoyan) family, shared with neighbours such as the Enxet and Enlhet. In the 1930s the Chaco War between Paraguay and Bolivia was fought across their land, and at the same time Mennonite settlers arrived in the central Chaco. Many Sanapaná settled near the Mennonite colonies and their missions, at La Esperanza together with the Lengua. Today they number a few thousand.
